title: God as Creator
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: God as Creator means that all things exist because God made them, owns them, sustains them, and gives them purpose. Creation belongs to Him and displays His glory.
summary: God as Creator means that all things exist because God made them, owns them, sustains them, and gives them purpose. Creation belongs to Him and displays His glory.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is not outside the work of creation; all things were made through Him and for Him. The Creator who made all things is also the Redeemer who restores what sin has broken.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture begins by revealing God as Creator. The heavens and earth are not eternal, accidental, or self-made. They exist because God spoke and brought them into being.

Because God created all things, all things belong to Him. The earth is the Lord’s and everything in it. Human beings are stewards, not owners of ultimate authority.

Creation reveals God’s power, wisdom, goodness, and glory. The Creator does not grow tired or weak. He sustains what He has made and remains Lord over it.

Christ is central to creation. All things were made through Him, and all things exist for God’s glory. The One through whom the world was made is also the One through whom God brings redemption and restoration.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
If God is not Creator, human life loses its foundation for dignity, purpose, worship, and accountability. People become free to invent meaning, but not able to create true meaning.

This doctrine reminds the weak and overlooked that their lives are not accidents. Every person is made by God, owned by God, seen by God, and accountable to God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor God as Creator in worship, stewardship, humility, and obedience. Treat creation as His, your body as His gift, and your life as entrusted to Him. Look to Christ as the One through whom creation exists and the One who restores what sin has damaged.
